attribution.note: Marcus's own words in his Substack post, stating as fact that Piltch replicated the gist of the results.

semantics.note: Matches the past-tense factual claim. The word 'independent' is a slight addition, but the contract limits it to Piltch generating his own results, which is fair.

contract.note: Plain reading of 'gist' is ordinary and fair: Piltch's own tests produce the central phenomenon, including with prompts that don't name characters. It doesn't require identical images or success every time.

evidence.note: Piltch's firsthand report from 2024-01-06. The neutral prompt 'animated toys' gave Woody and Buzz in Midjourney, and Bing gave R2D2. Some engines gave generic toys, which doesn't defeat 'gist'.
The authors' own article. It only identifies the finding being replicated, so it is not outcome evidence.

reviews.rationale: Piltch's report, published by the post date, documents his own tests. Prompts borrowed from Marcus and Southen that named no characters produced recognizable copyrighted characters (Toy Story figures, R2D2). That reproduces the central phenomenon. ChatGPT, Meta and SDXL returning generic toys, and Piltch's disclosed contact with the authors, don't undercut replicating the gist under the contract.
